title: Korean BBQ Onion Soy-Vinegar Dipping Sauce
shortDescription: The onion-soy dip is the tabletop steakhouse's bowl: sweet onion macerated in soy and vinegar until it turns translucent and half-pickled, served ice-cold beside the big beef cuts.
culturalContext: The onion-soy dip is the tabletop steakhouse's bowl: sweet onion macerated in soy and vinegar until it turns translucent and half-pickled, served ice-cold beside the big beef cuts. Where the scallion build (#SA04) is sharp and green, this one is sweet-rounded — onion's sugars soften the soy's salt and the vinegar turns it all bright — and its cold temperature against a just-off-the-grill rib is the entire reason it exists. It is also the easiest make-ahead on the site: ten minutes, a night in the fridge, better for it.

instructions.heading: Prepare onion cleanly
instructions.action: Rinse the whole onion exterior, peel, and slice thinly on a clean ready-to-eat board.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Onion slices are thin and clean.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep board and knife away from raw meat and seafood.

instructions.heading: Dissolve sauce
instructions.action: Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, water, sugar, and optional mustard until sugar dissolves.
instructions.safetyNote: Verify soy, wheat/gluten, and mustard-product labels.

instructions.heading: Chill briefly
instructions.action: Add onion, cover, and refrigerate 10 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Onion softens slightly but remains crisp.

instructions.heading: Portion individually
instructions.action: Spoon the needed sauce and onion into individual clean dipping dishes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Each diner has a separate portion.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not place the master container beside raw tabletop grilling.

instructions.heading: Protect the master batch
instructions.action: Return the covered uncontaminated master batch immediately to refrigeration.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Master sauce remains clean and cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Never return served sauce or onion to the master container.

instructions.heading: Discard contaminated portions
instructions.action: Discard every served portion contacted by raw food, shared utensils, hands, or used eating utensils.
instructions.safetyNote: Acid and soy sauce do not make raw-meat-contaminated dipping sauce safe.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is prepared without a grill.
visualDonenessCues: Master batch stays clean and refrigerated
foodSafetyNotes: Treat as a ready-to-eat refrigerated sauce.
Use clean tools and individual portions.
Discard any portion contacted by raw food or shared/used utensils.
Keep the master batch at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy and wheat/gluten; optional prepared mustard may add declared allergens, so verify its label.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
ingredientSourcing: Choose a firm onion without mold or soft spots and verify condiment labels.
makeAhead: Prepare up to 1 day ahead and keep covered and refrigerated.
storage: Keep the uncontaminated master batch at or below 40°F / 4°C and use within 3 days pending review.
reheating: Do not reheat; serve cold or cool.
leftovers: Discard all served portions and retain only uncontaminated refrigerated master sauce.
servingSuggestions: Serve in individual dishes with grilled foods.

faq.question: Can served sauce go back in the container?
Does vinegar make raw-meat contact safe?
faq.answer: No. Contaminated dipping sauce must be discarded.
